speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo; can you describe exactly how the sensation feels and how long each episode lasts?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. Since your dizziness is position-dependent, have you noticed any changes in your hearing, ringing in your ears, or fullness in your head alongside these episodes? Also, does turning over in bed or looking up specifically trigger the spinning sensation?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of position-dependent vertigo and age-related hearing loss, would you say the episodes are brief (lasting less than a minute) and triggered specifically by rolling over in bed or looking up? REQUEST IMAGES: Audiogram, Dix-Hallpike test video.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. No history of Meniere's disease, vestibular neuritis, or labyrinthitis. Social history: Retired school teacher. Lives alone. Non-smoker, occasional wine. Enjoys light gardening.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The clinical presentation of position-dependent vertigo in an older adult with a normal neurological exam and hearing history is classic for BPPV. I recommend starting with the Epley maneuver for treatment.
